_about: Hand labels for resume.jordan-rivera.md vs jobs.json. Kept apart from the inputs so the pipeline can never read the answers. `traps` are phrasings a keyword-rule pipeline is likely to get wrong; they're what Jev has to beat.

lakeshore-logistics:fixture:1001.why: Meets every required item (CS degree, Java and Python, SQL, Git, new grads welcome). Only misses AWS, which is nice-to-have.
traps: 'Java or Python' is one requirement satisfied by either, not two

prairie-health-tech:fixture:2002.why: React and REST are met. TypeScript is only partially met (has JavaScript). 1+ years professional is borderline: 3-month internship plus TA work.
traps: 'Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience' is met by the degree
JavaScript is partial evidence for TypeScript, not zero

northbrook-robotics:fixture:3003.why: Degree met, but misses Go/Rust, Kubernetes and 2+ years backend. Has adjacent evidence (Java backend, Docker, PostgreSQL).
traps: Docker is adjacent to Kubernetes but does not satisfy it
PostgreSQL is a bonus item, so it shouldn't raise the tier much

riverline-capital:fixture:4004.why: Misses the graduate-degree requirement, 3+ years of production ML, PyTorch and Spark. Has Python and a small scikit-learn project.
traps: A scikit-learn class project is not 'deploying models to production'
'MS or PhD' is not met by a B.S.

loop-defense-systems:fixture:5005.why: Requires an active TS/SCI clearance at start and 7+ years; the candidate has neither. Citizenship isn't stated on the resume, so it's unclear rather than unmet.
traps: Having C++ must not outweigh a hard blocker
Resume silence on citizenship means unclear, not does_not_meet
